cards.q: What is the SG rate?
aliases: how much does my employer pay
cards.a: 12% of qualifying earnings at minimum. 15% contributions tax is deducted from employer and concessional contributions.

sources.quote: The minimum SG percentage rate is 12%.

cards.q: What is the concessional contributions cap?
cards.a: $32,500 for 2026-27, across all funds. Includes SG, salary sacrifice and personal contributions claimed as a deduction.

sources.quote: A cap of $32,500 applies to concessional contributions during the 2026-27 financial year.

ato.quote: From 1 July 2026, the concessional contributions cap is $32,500.
Contributions count towards a cap in the year your super fund receives them.

cards.q: What happens if concessional contributions go over the cap?
cards.a: The excess is taxed at the member's marginal rate with a 15% non-refundable offset. Up to 85% can be released from super; anything left counts towards the non-concessional cap.

sources.quote: You can release up to 85% of your excess concessional contributions from your accumulation super account.

ato.quote: You can withdraw up to 85% of your ECC from your super fund to pay your income tax liability.

cards.q: What is the non-concessional contributions cap?
aliases: add extra money to my super
cards.a: $130,000 a year if total super balance at the previous 30 June was under $2.1 million; nil at or above $2.1 million.

sources.quote: you can generally contribute up to the annual non-concessional contributions cap of $130,000

ato.quote: From 1 July 2026, the non-concessional contributions cap is $130,000.
your non-concessional contributions cap is nil ($0) for the current financial year.

cards.q: How does the bring-forward rule work?
cards.a: Under 75 at any time in the year, up to three years' non-concessional cap at once. Total super balance at 30 June 2026: under $1.84m: $390,000 (three years); $1.84m to under $1.97m: $260,000 (two years); $1.97m to under $2.1m: $130,000; $2.1m+: nil.

sources.quote: Less than $1.84 million $390,000 Three years $1.84 million to less than $1.97 million $260,000 Two years
sources.label: Table: "Total super balance on 30 June 2026" against the non-concessional cap and bring-forward period

sources.quote: If you're under 75 years of age at any time during a financial year, you may be able to `bring forward' up to three years of non-concessional contributions in a financial year

ato.quote: If you're under 75 years of age at any time in a financial year, you're eligible to use the bring-forward arrangement in that financial year
This means you can make contributions up to 2 or 3 times the annual cap amount in the first year of the bring-forward period.

cards.q: What happens if non-concessional contributions go over the cap?
cards.a: Release the excess plus 85% of associated earnings (earnings taxed at marginal rate with a 15% offset), or leave it in and pay 47% on the excess.

sources.quote: If you choose not to release your excess non-concessional contributions they will remain in your super account and the excess will be taxed at 47%.

cards.q: Can unused concessional cap be carried forward?
cards.a: Yes, for up to five years, if total super balance was under $500,000 at the previous 30 June. Unused 2021-22 cap expires at the end of 2026-27.

sources.quote: you must have a total super balance of less than $500,000 as at 30 June of the financial year immediately preceding
For example, a 2021-22 unused cap amount that is not used by the end of 2026-27 will expire.

ato.quote: You can carry forward unused cap amounts from up to 5 previous financial years, including when you were not a member of a super fund.
Your available carry-forward contribution amounts are shown on ATO online services

cards.detail: Order: this year's general cap fills first, then unused amounts, oldest year first (ATO).

cards.q: When must a notice of intent to claim a deduction be lodged?
cards.a: Acknowledged before the earlier of lodging that year's tax return or the end of the following financial year. And before the contributions are rolled over, withdrawn, or used to start a pension.
cards.detail: Online: log in, Manage account, Notice of intent. Lodge it before any contribution split too.

sources.quote: You must submit your claim (and we must acknowledge receipt in writing) before whichever of the following occurs first
In addition, UniSuper must still hold these contributions and can't have begun paying a superannuation income stream based on all or part of these contributions

cards.q: What happens to contributions claimed as a deduction?
cards.a: They become concessional contributions, generally taxed 15% in the fund, and count towards the concessional cap.

sources.quote: Any contributions on which you claim a tax deduction will be treated as concessional contributions

cards.q: How does salary sacrifice work?
cards.a: Arranged through the employer's payroll. It's a concessional contribution (15% tax) and counts in some income tests, including the co-contribution and Division 293.

sources.quote: Salary sacrifice is organised through your employer's payroll department.

cards.q: What if we don't have the member's TFN?
aliases: what if i have no tfn
cards.a: An extra 32% (47% total) may be taken from assessable contributions, and member, spouse and co-contributions can't be accepted. Provide the TFN within three financial years to recover the extra tax.

sources.quote: If you haven't provided your TFN, an additional tax of 32% may be deducted (totalling 47%) from assessable contributions
If you haven't provided us with your TFN, we can't accept certain types of contributions (e.g. member contributions and spouse contributions).

cards.q: How does the government co-contribution work?
cards.a: For total income up to $49,293 (2026-27), the government adds 50c per $1 of non-concessional contributions, up to $500. It phases out at $64,293. Paid automatically the next year; needs a TFN.

sources.quote: If your total income is $49,293 per annum or less for 2026-27
before phasing out completely if you earn $64,293 per annum or more

ato.quote: be less than 71 years old at the end of the financial year
The minimum co-contribution payment is $20 and the maximum is $500.

cards.q: What is LISTO?
cards.a: 15% of concessional contributions, up to $500, for adjusted taxable income up to $37,000. The ATO pays it into super automatically.

sources.quote: The amount of the offset for eligible members is 15% of the total amount of eligible concessional (before-tax) contributions for the year up to a maximum payment of $500.

ato.quote: If you earn up to $37,000 a year, you may be eligible to receive a low income super tax offset (LISTO) payment of up to $500.

cards.q: How does the spouse contribution tax offset work?
cards.a: 18% offset on up to $3,000 contributed for a spouse: maximum $540 if the spouse's income is $37,000 or less, phasing out at $40,000. Not available if the spouse's total super balance is $2.1m+ or they're over their non-concessional cap.

sources.quote: The maximum spouse contribution tax offset of $540 is available if you make contributions of up to $3,000 on behalf of your spouse

ato.quote: The tax offset amount reduces when your spouse's income is greater than $37,000. It phases out when your spouse’s income reaches $40,000.

cards.q: How does contribution splitting work?
cards.a: Up to the lesser of 85% of concessional contributions or the concessional cap, to a spouse under 60, or 60 to 64 and not retired. Usually last year's contributions, by 30 June; once a year. Lodge any notice of intent first.
cards.detail: Can be done in the same year if the whole balance is leaving. May be refused if the balance would fall below $6,000. Non-concessional contributions, rollovers and co-contributions can't be split. Once transferred, the split money belongs to the spouse and is preserved in their account; {{split-cap:it still counts towards the member's own concessional cap}}.

sources.quote: The maximum amount of contributions that can be split each financial year is the lesser of: 85% of your concessional contributions, and the concessional contributions cap applicable to you.
You can't split contributions with your spouse if they're age 65 or over.
we may refuse the application if it would result in your accumulation balance falling below $6,000

ato.quote: You can ask your super fund to transfer to your spouse, up to 85% of a financial year's taxed splittable contributions.
Note: You can only apply once to split contributions made to a particular super fund in a financial year.

cards.q: What is a downsizer contribution?
cards.a: From age 55, after owning the home 10+ years: up to $300,000 each ($600,000 a couple) from the sale. Doesn't count to the caps or need a total super balance test, but counts to the transfer balance cap. ATO form plus payment, generally within 90 days of settlement.

sources.quote: If you're aged 55 or older and have owned your house for at least 10 years, you may be able to contribute up to $300,000 ($600,000 per couple) into super from the proceeds of selling your home.
generally within 90 days of settlement

ato.quote: A downsizer contribution does not count towards contributions caps (concessional or non-concessional).
You contribute within 90 days of receiving the home sale proceeds (usually at settlement) unless you apply for, and we grant you an extension of time.

cards.q: Can COVID early release be put back?
cards.a: Yes, up to the amount withdrawn, until 30 June 2030, without counting to the non-concessional cap. No deduction can be claimed. ATO form before or with the payment.

sources.quote: This is only available until 30 June 2030, and can't exceed the amount you withdrew under the scheme.

cards.q: Is super paid on government Paid Parental Leave?
cards.a: Yes, the ATO may pay it at the SG rate. It's taxed 15% and counts to the concessional cap.

sources.quote: The ATO may pay superannuation on government funded Parental Leave Pay to your super account.

cards.q: Which contributions can be accepted at what age?
cards.a: Under 75: all types (downsizer from 55). 75 and over: only mandated employer contributions and downsizer; voluntary ones until 28 days after the end of the month the member turns 75.

sources.quote: We can accept contributions up to 28 days after the end of the month in which you turn 75.

cards.q: Is there a work test for claiming a deduction?
cards.a: Yes, for ages 67 to 74: 40 hours' work within 30 consecutive days in the year the contribution is made. The ATO checks it at tax time.

sources.quote: Individuals aged 67-74 are required to meet the work test (or exemption) to claim a deduction on personal contributions.

cards.q: What is Division 293 tax?
cards.a: An extra 15% on concessional contributions when income plus concessional contributions exceed $250,000, applied to the lower of the contributions or the amount over $250,000. Paid personally or released from super.

sources.quote: Division 293 super contributions of more than $250,000 within a financial year, an additional tax of 15%

ato.quote: Division 293 tax is charged at 15% of the excess over the threshold or the taxable super contributions, whichever is less.

cards.q: What is Division 296 tax?
cards.a: From 1 July 2026: 15% on the share of earnings relating to a total super balance over $3 million, plus 10% more on the share over $10 million. The ATO assesses it.

sources.quote: If your TSB exceeds $3 million, you will be subject to Division 296 tax of 15% on the proportion of earnings relating to your TSB that exceeds $3 million.

cards.q: How does the First Home Super Saver scheme work?
cards.a: Voluntary contributions since 1 July 2017 (up to $15,000 a year, $50,000 total) can be released for a first home. The member requests a determination from the ATO. Not SG, not DB.

sources.quote: You can make up to $15,000 of voluntary (concessional or non-concessional) contributions to your accumulation super per financial year and up to $50,000 in total under the scheme.

ato.quote: How much you can access, the maximum release amounts and when you need to request a determination.

cards.q: Can UniSuper accept a UK pension or KiwiSaver transfer?
cards.a: No, UniSuper can't accept transfers from UK pension or KiwiSaver accounts.

sources.quote: Please note that UniSuper is unable to accept transfers from UK pension or KiwiSaver accounts.

cards.q: Is tax payable on a rollover in?
cards.a: No, unless it contains an untaxed element (for example from some public sector funds), which is taxed 15% on arrival.

sources.quote: An untaxed element transferred into UniSuper attracts 15% contributions tax.

cards.q: Can a member choose UniSuper for their employer contributions?
cards.a: Usually, if eligible for choice. Give the employer the Super choice form (or the pre-filled form from the online account). Without a choice, contributions may go to the member's stapled fund. Enterprise agreements from 1 January 2021 must follow the member's choice.
cards.detail: DBD members aren't eligible for choice while in a DBD-eligible role.

sources.quote: If you're covered by an Enterprise Agreement made on or after 1 January 2021, your employer must pay your SG contributions in accordance with your choice of fund election
If you don't choose a fund, most employers are required to make SG contributions to your stapled fund (if you have one).
